sense.text:
“From Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations.” So from David to Babylon is fourteen generations, and before the Babylonian captivity there was the Assyrian captivity.

“And from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations.” From Babylon to Christ you have more captivities: Persia-Media, the Greek captivity, and then Rome. Christ was born in the Roman captivity. This verse is talking about captivities, and that is why we needed a saviour.

precepts.why:
“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” Why do we need saving? Because of verse 17, the captivities.

Sin is the reason we went into the Babylonian captivity. Sin is the reason we went into the Persian-Median captivity, the Greek captivity, and finally the Roman captivity. And here we are today. Sin has always been our problem.

Christ “answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” That verse proves he is only for the Israelites.

The angel said his name would be Jesus and that he would save his people, and Christ says the same thing here. There are no contradictions in the Bible. The only contradictions are your Christianity and your imams.

sense.text:
People say the people in the land of Israel are the Jews, but that is not what the Bible says. “Immediately after the tribulation of those days”: Christ is telling us there will be tribulation.

“The stars shall fall from heaven”: the stars falling from heaven are missiles. “And the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: that is countries and nations warring against each other.

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Watch whether they go to the land of Israel to gather this people. They don't.

So what is Christ letting us know? The Israelites would not be in a land. The Israelites would be scattered worldwide, in the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

precepts.why:
Who is the elect? People will say anybody that worships. But God says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” That is the elect: Israel.

So when Christ sends his angels to gather “his elect from the four winds”, it is the Israelites, scattered from one end of heaven to the other, that they are sent to gather.

sense.text: Before the angels can get the elect, there is a message here. “He shall call to the heavens from above”: the heavens he calls to are the angels. “And to the earth”: the earth is you and I. “That he may judge his people.”

“Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice.

This is what we read in Matthew 24, where Christ tells his angels to gather the elect. And the message for us on earth is the same: gather the saints together. It is the commandment to the angels and to the prophets on earth. We are not supposed to be looking for other races, other nationalities. Only the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.why:
Who are the saints? “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The children of Israel are the saints.

So when God says “Gather my saints together unto me”, he is commanding the gathering of the children of Israel, the only people that made a covenant with him by sacrifice.

sense.text:
“For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour”: he is the Holy One of Israel and he is our saviour, so we know the subject is the children of Israel.

“I gave Egypt for thy ransom”: he killed the Egyptian army for our ransom. “Ethiopia and Seba for thee”: he destroyed the Ethiopian military and Seba, that is Somalia, for us.

“Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable”: we have been honourable, and we have to learn that honour. “And I have loved thee.”

“Therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” God is saying he has to kill nations to deliver us from captivity. The same way he destroyed ancient Egypt, Ethiopia and the Sabeans, he must do it again: he must destroy nations for our deliverance. If you say you don't want God to destroy anybody, then you don't read the Bible. You don't know what you are into.

“Fear not: for I am with thee.” The Lord tells us fear not, he is with us. “I will bring thy seed from the east”: he is going to bring the Israelites that are in the eastern side of the world. “And gather thee from the west”: that is us here in the western hemisphere.

“I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back”: he speaks to the Israelites in the north and to the Israelites in the south. “Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”

“Even every one that is called by my name.” That is why we have to teach our people: you are the Israelites the Bible speaks of. “For I have created him for my glory, I have formed him; yea, I have made him.”

Did the apostles change anything and go gather everybody on the planet? No. “There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Jews, Israelites, came from every nation under heaven.

“Every man heard them speak in his own language.” That is speaking in tongues.

Why didn't God just have them teach in Hebrew? Because Hebrew was not the first language of these Israelites. Their first language was the language of the countries they were born in. God wanted to make sure there would be no misunderstanding, so he anointed the brothers with the Holy Spirit to speak in their own language, their first language, so they would understand exactly what was being said.

“Are not all these which speak Galileans?” In Galilee they only spoke Hebrew. So the Israelites that came from these different countries were saying, Don't they only speak Hebrew? It is like America, where the Americans pretty much only speak English.

“How hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born?” Because they were born in other countries.

“Parthians, and Medes”: that is the Persia-Media captivity. Parthia is Persia, and the Medes are modern-day Iran. “Elamites” is India and Pakistan. “Mesopotamia” is Iraq today, what was called Babylon back then.

“Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia, Phrygia, and Pamphylia”: Asia here is Asia Minor, and all those names are the region of modern-day Turkey. “Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene”: this is Africa. “And strangers of Rome.”

“Jews and proselytes”: a proselyte is a convert. Those were men and women who were not keeping the law of Moses but converted back to it. That is what proselyte means here.

“Cretes and Arabians”: some of us came from the Arab captivity, and Crete is Greece, from the Greek captivity. Some of our people stayed over there. “We do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God”: there was no misunderstanding of what was being said.

“Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine”: they said they were all drunk. But Peter answered, “these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day.” The third hour of the day is nine o’clock in the morning. Who gets drunk at nine in the morning? Nobody does that.

Those Israelites were there for the feast of Pentecost, and then they all went back to their respective countries wherein they were born.
“Paul called unto him the disciples”: remember, the word disciple means students.
“He came into Greece, And there abode three months”: he stayed in Greece three months. “And when the Jews laid wait for him”: these were the envious and hateful Jews of our own people.

“And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus”, that is Timothy, “and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.”

Paul had a team of men that he travelled with to teach the gospel. Most of these men we don't see named much in Acts, except Timothy, but they were there helping Paul and Timothy spread the gospel. It is nothing different than what we are doing today.

This is what the churches mess up on and are always confused about. “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.” This was the result of breaking God's commandments and sinning.

“And there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” We would worship wood, the wooden cross, and stone, the stone of Allah. That is what the Kaaba stone is.

precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” Even in the New Testament it tells you the twelve tribes were scattered.

They would not be in the land of Israel. They would be scattered among all people, from one end of the earth to the other, just as Moses said.

sense.text:
Captain Shay said in the war room that what we did this past Passover is like throwing a stone into the water: it has a ripple effect. It starts small and goes out. We land in these countries and teach the gospel, and there is a spiritual ripple effect. You might not see it, but the effects will be made manifest.

“They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them.” We were commanded to destroy the Jebusites, the Philistines, the Canaanites and the Amalekites. We didn't do that.

“But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” Our people on the continent of Africa mingled among those Philistines, Canaanites, Jebusites and Hittites, and learned their works.

Our people on this side of the world didn't mingle with the Hamites. Who did they mingle with? Esau, the so-called white man. That is why you've got the change in the complexion and the hair that they've got. I don't see why a negro can't understand that.

“There shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” When you bring this verse out on the street, highlight the word Gentiles: the subject matter is the Gentiles.

Christ is that ensign, and today that is the Bible, because Christ is not walking around with us. Come back to the word of God. To it, the Bible, shall the Gentiles seek.

“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” Where are they left?

“From Assyria”: that is Turkey, that whole region. “From Egypt”: Africa. “From Pathros”: Sudan, Africa. “From Cush”: Ethiopia, Africa. “From Elam”: Iran, Iraq, Pakistan and India. “From Shinar”: Iraq. “From Hamath”: Syria, where you've got the Afro-Syrians. “And from the islands of the sea”: Puerto Rico, Jamaica, Haiti, and the Melanesian islands, thousands of islands, most of them inhabited.

“He shall set up an ensign for the nations”: those Gentiles, those nations, are the remnant of Israel. “And shall assemble the outcasts of Israel”: that lets you know the Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel. “And gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.”

So saying that the people in the land are our people is erroneous and non-biblical.

“From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia”: now we are talking about the continent of Africa. The Blue Nile encompasses Ethiopia, and beyond that goes toward West Africa, South Africa and North Africa.

“Even the daughter of my dispersed”: dispersed means scattered. A large portion of God's scattered people are on the continent of Africa.

“For then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride.” That is the pastors, the Christians: they rejoice in our pride, meaning our sin. People rejoice in us going against God's commandments: the churches, the Democrats, the Republicans. That is called pride, and God says he will take them away from us.

“And thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain”: the holy mountain is the land of Israel.

“I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people.” The elect over there are an afflicted and poor people. We have gone throughout Africa on this past journey keeping the feast of unleavened bread and Passover. Are they not afflicted and poor? They are afflicted and very poor.

“And they shall trust in the name of the Lord”: we have to teach them to trust in the name of the Lord.

“The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity”: so they must be taught. This is what we are going out there for. They shall not do iniquity because they are being taught the commandments.

“Nor speak lies”: no, Jesus is not white. No, he was not born December 25th. No, we are not to pray to Mary. No, we are not to pray to the ancestors. “For they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.”

So what's our problem? Sin has always been the problem. Our sin is our unbelief. Breaking God's commandments is a sign of unbelief, and that has always been our problem.

precepts.why:
To prove what pride is: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God.”

So when Zephaniah says God will take away “them that rejoice in thy pride”, that pride is our departing from God, our going against his commandments. Those who rejoice in it are the churches and the politicians who rejoice in us not keeping God's commandments, and God says he will take them out from among us.

sense.text:
“But this is a people robbed and spoiled.” As a race, as a people, we are robbed and spoiled. Other nations go throughout Africa, where the people are literally walking on gold and diamonds, but the only ones that benefit from the gold, the diamonds, the bauxite and the lithium are the other nations.

“They are all of them snared in holes”: holes like Christianity, a big hole. Presbyterian, Lutheran, Catholic, Islam: those are the holes we've been trapped in. “And they are hid in prison houses”: the lands we now live in are our prison houses. “They are for a prey, and none delivereth”: nobody delivers us.

“For a spoil, and none saith, Restore.” You saw what happened at the UN: they said the transatlantic slave trade was the worst thing in human history, and America, Argentina and Israel said they didn't agree. They couldn't even bring up reparations. None of them is saying give them back what is owed them, give them back the land taken from them.

“Who gave Jacob for a spoil, and Israel to the robbers? did not the Lord”: yes, it was the Lord that did that. Why? “He against whom we have sinned.” Because we have sinned.

“For they would not walk in his ways, neither were they obedient unto his law”: our people, our twelve tribes, would not walk in his ways, and we were not obedient unto his law.

“Therefore he hath poured upon him the fury of his anger, and the strength of battle.” That is what slavery is all about. That is what Jim Crow, redlining and the black codes were all about. That is what our current situation is all about.

“It hath set him on fire round about, yet he knew not; and it burned him, yet he laid it not to heart.” Although we got burnt up, we didn't lay it to heart. As a race we don't stop and think that we are going through all these problems because of our sins.

Even the white man's own scholars saw it. Reading The Jewish Mystique: they divided and conquered us, burned our records, and handed us our religion, our self-image and our ambitions, so the white man gave us everything we have right now, and the only society we know, white society, doesn't even accept our people. Our culture is found in the Bible, but our people don't know that. Our code of conduct is in the Bible, God's moral, civil and ceremonial laws, but we don't believe keeping it leads to redemption; that's why they say, You can't judge me, we're under grace and not the law. We don't realize our sufferings are a direct result of disobeying our heavenly Father, and the white man realized that our redemption comes through studying and obeying God's law.

Instead we think our help comes from outside secular, worldly forces: we need economics, we need the white man to help us, we need to move, talk and operate like the white man in this system. We try to coerce white folks into giving us money, jobs and education, and into repairing the damage done. We can never get true independence as long as we're looking to outside secular forces to help us.

Now we see brothers and sisters waking up worldwide. “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost”: the comforter is the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit. “He shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

Why would we need to remember the things Christ said? Because we would be made to forget. We forgot through slavery: the nations annihilated our twelve tribes, burned our records and beat us into submission, and we forgot what Christ said.

And what did Christ say? That he would gather his elect from the four corners of the earth. That he was only sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The Holy Spirit would cause us to remember these things. If you don't remember those things, you don't have the Holy Spirit on you.

precepts.why:
Christ also said: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” That is one of the things the Holy Spirit brings back to our remembrance.

The Comforter brings to remembrance whatsoever Christ said, and Christ said to keep his commandments. If you don't remember that, you don't have the Holy Spirit on you.

sense.text: “Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen.” God only chose Israel.
“Thus saith the Lord that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee”: the Lord will help us. “Fear not, O Jacob, my servant”: Jacob is our father, and he is telling us, fear not.

What is he going to do for us? “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty.” Thirsty for what? Thirsty for the truth. If you are thirsty for the truth, the Lord has prophesied he would pour water, his word, upon you.

“And floods upon the dry ground”: the floods also represent the word of God, and the dry ground is these places wherein we dwell. “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed”: thy seed, thy people. “And my blessing upon thine offspring”: thy children.
“And they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses.” The Israelites are waking up. This is what we are looking at now: we are springing up worldwide like grass.

In our redemption, coming back to the truth, “One shall say, I am the Lord’s”: we are going to acknowledge we are the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

“And another shall call himself by the name of Jacob”: another takes on a new name, an alias, an aka, beside the name he has now. “And another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel”: another says, I'm changing my surname; my surname is Israel from now on.

Those are three different categories in verse 5, and all three are Israelites waking up.

precepts.why:
So we know what the water is: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.” The water represents the word of God.

So when God says “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”, he is saying I will pour the word of God upon them that are thirsty for the truth.

sense.text:
Now, as we are waking up: “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord.” He is telling us to flee from North America. That is the land of the north.

“For I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: all Israel scattered like the four winds of heaven, like we read in Matthew 24.

“Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Many scriptures tell us that Zion represents the twelve tribes, but in this context Zion is Judah: deliver yourself, Judah.

The key is “that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” The daughter of Babylon is Edom, the so-called white folks. Judah would live among them, in the land of the north. That is not all of Judah, because we already read that Judah was dispersed like all the other tribes. God is pinpointing a particular group of Judah that would be in the land of the north.
“After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” We are God's favourite.

precepts.why:
Which Zion is it? “But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” That is Zion right there: the tribe of Judah.

So “Deliver thyself, O Zion” is talking about Judah. Deliver yourself, Judah.

Who is the daughter of Babylon? “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” The word rase means destroy it.

Then: “O daughter of Babylon.” Notice what it is calling the children of Edom, the so-called white folks: the daughter of Babylon.

So when Zechariah says Zion “dwellest with the daughter of Babylon”, it is letting you know Judah would live among Edom in the land of the north.

sense.text:
Moses is prophesying here: “And this is the blessing of Judah.” “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah”: the voice of Judah is the teachings of Judah. “And bring him unto his people”: bring Judah to the other eleven tribes.

“Let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies”: help Judah from his enemies as he is teaching the other tribes. God is letting you know that in these last days the tribe of Judah would be raised up first, and Judah would go out and teach the other tribes. Judah would do the research and study to find out who and where the other tribes of Israel are.

precepts.why:
Judah was raised up first: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The prophecy is, I will raise up Judah first.

So the springing up like grass in Isaiah 44 starts with Judah, and then, as Deuteronomy 33 says, Judah goes out and teaches the other tribes.

sense.text:
“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?” How could they call on the almighty God that only loves them, when they have not believed in that God? Our people believed in a strange God, a Eurocentric God. We are the only race that has a god that does not look like us.

“And how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” Because we have been following a strange God all our lives. Why is that God strange? He doesn't look like you, he has no laws, statutes or commandments, and he whipped you in slavery. Yet we run on Sunday morning and pray faithfully to the same white man that shot us down in the streets and raped our mothers and fathers.

“And how shall they hear without a preacher?” Preacher means prophet. To preach means to foretell, like in the beginning. That is a prophet.

“And how shall they preach, except they be sent?” That is what this Passover has been all about. That is why we are sending you, brothers. Not just because we like you: if you don't have a good reputation, a good name in this, we are not sending you. Some brothers went to other countries and showed their ass and had to be demoted. One brother got put out for going to the other side of the world gossiping, stirring up and murmuring against people.

“As it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” Travelling from country to country, nation to nation, preaching the gospel of peace is a beautiful thing. And the glad tidings are: you are the Israelites, Christ died for you and only you, your race and only your race, and he is only coming back to save our race. That is the good news.

Brothers don't realize the impact they have on people. You come from another country and teach them that they are the Israelites. It might not set in that night; it might be the night after, or the week after, but it is going to marinate in their souls. It has a spiritual ripple effect.

precepts.why:
The God we serve is not the same God as the white man's. “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory.” That white Jesus is a strange god.

“And he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain.” The white man divided Africa for gain. That is what the Bible says he did.

So when Paul asks how they shall call on him in whom they have not believed, it is because our people have been believing in and obeying a strange god.

sense.text:
“These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles”: in this verse that means the other eleven tribes. Don't deal with them yet. “And into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”: the Samaritans are the northern kingdom, the tribe of Ephraim. Don't even deal with them.

Why? Because it wasn't time for them yet. Remember Zechariah 12: Judah is raised up first. We have always taught this; people just keep forgetting.

“But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” That starts with Judah. Judah first.

And Christ did go to Samaria and taught the Samaritans for a few days, the Samaritan woman in John 4, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them. Don't be confused.
“And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ sent out, dispatched, the twelve disciples to go forth and teach.

precepts.why:
“Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” Only to Judah. In the beginning the work was primarily dealing with Judah.

That is what Christ meant when he told the twelve not to go into the way of the Gentiles: Judah first.

Watch what Paul says: “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?” Even us, the tribe of Benjamin and all the other tribes. Not of Judah only, but also of the Gentiles, the other eleven tribes.

They were perverting Zechariah 12:7, where the Lord saves the tents of Judah first, as if it were only Judah. It starts with Judah, as Christ commanded in Matthew 10, but the calling goes on to the Gentiles, the rest of the tribes.

sense.text: Christ sending out the twelve was nothing new. “He took away the high places and groves out of Judah”: Jehoshaphat took away all those false idols, those gods, those little churches, those groves, and destroyed them.
“In the third year of his reign he sent to his princes”, Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethaneel and Michaiah, “to teach in the cities of Judah.” And with them he sent Levites and priests.

“And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them”: they had the Bible with them. “And went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.”

What Christ did was not new. King Jehoshaphat did the same thing. In his time our people were worshipping Molech, Chemosh, Baal, all those false gods, and he said, tear down those churches, those groves, and I need you men to go throughout Judah and teach. That is what they did, and that is the same thing Christ did in Matthew 10.

The old Biblical and Theological Dictionary bears it out: at times itinerants, princes, priests and Levites, were sent through all the country to carry the book of the law and teach in the cities. That's what we read in Chronicles. Those discourses were preached in camps, in courts, in streets, schools, cities and villages. Don't let people tell you there are no camps in the Bible. That's what we're doing.

Acts 10 is regarding the northern kingdom. “There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius”: Caesarea was a city in the land of Manasseh. Look it up in your Bible dictionary.

“A centurion of the band called the Italian band”: people read that and say he was white. No, he was not. He was an Israelite of the tribe of Manasseh.

“A devout man”: devoted to God almighty. “And one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” These are not the other nations. This is not another race. This is Israel.

precepts.why:
Remember Acts 11, the next chapter: “they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” They were only teaching the Jews, the tribe of Judah.

In Acts 10 that vision came to Peter, and Peter only. Then in the very next chapter, Acts 11:19, they were still preaching only to the Jews, the tribe of Judah.

“Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”: talking to Judah. “But seeing ye put it from you”: the scribes and them were rejecting it. “And judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.”

The word went to Judah first, and then they turned to the Gentiles. So who are the Gentiles?

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” See what they call the northern kingdom: Gentiles.

So when you read Acts 10 with Cornelius of Caesarea in Manasseh, it is talking of the northern kingdom, the Gentiles that are Israel.

sense.text:
Peter “saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”, with “all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.” A voice said, “Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” But Peter said, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.”

Peter was in a trance. He saw a vision, and verse 28 is the breakdown, where he explains what it means.

“Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew”, Judah, “to keep company, or come unto one of another nation.” That might throw you off, because Christians use it. But the other nation is the kingdom of Israel.

“But God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” That is what the vision was about: Cornelius and his family.

precepts.why:
Write it down as a precept: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.”

The kingdom of Judah was called a nation, and the kingdom of Israel, Ephraim and the rest, was called a nation. Two nations, two separate kingdoms. So when Peter speaks of “one of another nation”, he means the kingdom of Israel.

“Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” A Christian will stop you right there. But read the next verse.

“The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ.” That verse tells you Cornelius and his kinfolk are the children of Israel.

sense.text: Acts 15 is explaining, discussing, Acts 10. “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written.”

“After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up.” There was a split in the kingdom of Israel: Judah, Benjamin and Levi on one side, Ephraim and the rest on the other. They considered themselves two different nations. That is the tabernacle of David that is fallen down.

So what is he talking about? The regathering of the twelve tribes, the two kingdoms coming back together. That is what Acts 10 is about, and that is what Acts 15 is reminiscing on: God bringing the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom back together.

“A man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship.” This man came to Jerusalem to worship.
He “was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet.” Not only did he come to Jerusalem to worship, he was reading the book of Isaiah.

Philip asked him, “Understandest thou what thou readest?” And he said, “How can I, except some man should guide me?” That is a profound statement.

They were only preaching to the Jews at this time. So this man was a Jew. It is easy to understand.

precepts.why:
Read for the third time so it is not forgotten: “they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” This was before God told Paul and Barnabas to go to the northern kingdom Israelites.

Who were they teaching? Jews only. So the man of Ethiopia that Philip was sent to, a few chapters before, was a Jew.

sense.text: The eunuch said, How can I understand except some man should guide me? “My son, if thou wilt, thou shalt be taught: and if thou wilt apply thy mind, thou shalt be prudent.” Notice he keeps saying if. If is a two-letter word with a big meaning. If thou wilt apply thy mind: study, pray, apply.
“If thou love to hear, thou shalt receive understanding: and if thou bow thine ear, thou shalt be wise.”

“Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave unto him that is wise. Be willing to hear every godly discourse; and let not the parables of understanding escape thee. And if thou seest a man of understanding, get thee betimes unto him, and let thy foot wear the steps of his door.”

“Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.”

So when you pray for wisdom, brothers and sisters, God will only give it at your own desire. If you only look in the Bible today, on the Sabbath, once a week, your desire is, Lord, I really don't want it that much. You are not occupying your time with his word. God will only increase your understanding at your own desire.

precepts.why:
“Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly.” Not by constraint, not by force. We are not forcing any of you to do any work. If you don't want to travel, that's fine; be that local prophet. Sometimes brothers don't even want to be a man of rank. You can be a member. It's okay. God only wants those who have a willing mind.

“Not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind”: not for money, not because you want to get paid. “Neither as being lords over God’s heritage”: we are not in this truth to rule and dominate other brothers and sisters and control their lives. “But being ensamples to the flock”: ensample means example. Be an example to the flock of God.

It goes with Ecclesiasticus 6: God gives wisdom at your own desire, and he wants those who serve willingly.

sense.text: “All these trust to their hands: and every one is wise in his work.” This whole chapter is talking about brothers who love their worldly job, their secular job, and that is all they occupy themselves with. They don't occupy themselves with studying, praying and applying the scriptures. Your job in the world is all you really care about.

“Without these cannot a city be inhabited”: without your work the city couldn't be inhabited. “And they shall not dwell where they will, nor go up and down”: you can't dwell where you want to, nor go up and down.

“They shall not be sought for in publick counsel”: because you are so occupied in your work, you will never be sought for in public counsel. When things are going down, we don't want to hear your opinion, because your opinion is your job. You don't know the scriptures. “Nor sit high in the congregation”: you will have no rank. If you want to be a member, be a member; there is nothing wrong with that.

“They shall not sit on the judges’ seat, nor understand the sentence of judgment.” You are the brother who will always be confused. Deacon Abiel and Officer Laab had a skit on today's show about the brother who says, I don't agree with that judgment. You don't agree because you don't know the scriptures. All you know is your job.

“They cannot declare justice and judgment; and they shall not be found where parables are spoken.” When brothers are going over parables, you are nowhere around, because you could care less. If the shoe fits, brother, wear it.

“But they will maintain the state of the world, and all their desire is in the work of their craft.” You will maintain the state of the world, Babylon the great. That is where your occupation is, and that is all you care about.

precepts.why:
Why don't you understand when judgments are passed? “Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.”

Now you know why you are always confused. When the leadership makes a judgment, you don't agree, and you don't agree in silence. But the Bible says you're evil. You are an evil ninja.

sense.text: Here is the flip side: the brother “that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.”

“He will keep the sayings of the renowned men”: renowned means famous. “And where subtil parables are, he will be there also”: where those parables are, you will see that brother right there, wanting to learn.

“He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.” A secret of a grave sentence is like when Christ asked the Pharisees about David: The Lord said unto my Lord, sit thou on my right hand until I make thy enemies thy footstool. If he is David's son, why does David call him my Lord? Most people can't even explain that.

“He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes.” As we have travelled, brothers have sat before dignitaries: a vice president of a country, mayors, governors, major politicians. We don't show everything. In Uganda, when we sat down with the vice president, his assistant told us to sit ourselves down in rank, and that none of us should speak until the vice president spoke; then, starting from the most senior, we could speak on down. That is what this scripture is talking about.

“He will travel through strange countries; for he hath tried the good and the evil among men.” That sounds familiar. So don't be surprised when we decline your debate, brothers online. If we are sitting down with vice presidents, mayors and governors, why should we waste our time arguing with you? We're not sitting down debating and arguing with you, because you really don't believe. That's why you stay in your mama's house and you're a keyboard warrior all day. IUIC is doing big things, and arguing is beneath us. It's a waste of our time.

In Liberia, in a big church of all black people, there were five Edomites sitting there, CIA, monitoring the former president who is up for reelection. They had the nerve to ask the brothers why Israel United in Christ was there, and they followed the brothers all the way to where they were meeting the former president. We are meeting people of high status, sharing the gospel, and people are believing.

“He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and will pray before the most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.” That is why we send out the morning prayer every morning at sunrise.

“When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding.” So you can't rush this. You cannot rush your understanding. “He shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks unto the Lord in his prayer.”
“He shall direct his counsel and knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate. He shall shew forth that which he hath learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord.”

precepts.why:
“And Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God. And all the people answered, Amen, Amen, with lifting up their hands.” Then Jeshua, Bani and the rest, “and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law: and the people stood in their place.” The Levites caused the people to understand what the law meant.

“So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.”

That is the man who shows forth what he has learned. They had schools for this, the schools of the prophets, and the students were called sons of the prophets: not because they were the actual sons of the former prophets, but because they walked in the same footsteps, obedient and learning. What IUIC is doing is nothing new. The schools across the world follow the same protocol as here in the States: learning the laws of God, how to teach, how to preach, how to conduct yourself, and how to stand before great men.

sense.text:
“Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple”, they came and said, “Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do; and we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.” You can read that history in 2 Kings 17.

Notice the word it gives them: adversaries, which means enemies. The forefathers discerned in the spirit that these were not their friends.
“Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us.”

“Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building.” These were the adversaries who made it seem like they wanted to help us. They were so interested in helping the Israelites rebuild the temple wall.

“And hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.” Our adversaries hired lowlife people to trouble the men that were building back the temple wall.

precepts.why:
1 Esdras tells the same history in a little more detail. “Then Zorobabel and Jesus”, and Jesus is Joshua, “and the chief of the families of Israel said unto them, It is not for us and you to build together an house unto the Lord our God.”

“But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building; And by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions”: they had secret plots against us, and they were persuading people to go against us. It is the same today. In India there are negroes who hate this gospel, going to the police and to the pastors and preachers, saying, We've got to stop those Israelites and shut down that school.

“So they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius.” We could not rebuild for two years; that is how much trouble the other nations gave us. You might think that will never happen in these times, but it does. The FBI put informants in black groups at the very beginning, so they could position themselves ahead of the growth of these groups. Be mindful of brothers and sisters who just up and disappear, then turn up in the congregation in another country with no counsel. If you are going to an IUIC school, let us know. Don't just pop up.
